query: Explique-moi les migrations background du monolithe : pourquoi db/migrate-background, et pourquoi le code qui en dépend attend une PR suivante.
expected_behavior: Opens real files before writing anything: at minimum .claude/rules/db/migrations-safety.md, .claude/rules/background-migration-code-ordering.md, and at least one migration under db/migrate-background/
Asks the prerequisite question (step 4) in exactly one AskUserQuestion, multi-select, with three to five background concepts, none of which is the subject itself
States a spine sentence in its reply before building the page, phrased as a correction of what the reader believes
The page answers why it exists and when you meet it BEFORE explaining the mechanism
The page answers whether this is still the way we do it (step 5, question 7), or says plainly that nothing in the repo states a direction
The page explains how a background migration is undone, not only how it runs
scripts/audit-page.py exits 0 on the published file
No section exceeds eight body paragraphs
The page has at least as many tables as half its sections
At least one diagram shows the mechanism rather than the location of files
The reply tells the user the Artifact is private until they share it
The reply names two or three specific points it compressed and offers to expand them
known_failure_modes: Claiming migrations run in batches - they do not; a large backfill belongs in a rake task (migrations-safety.md)
Describing the intermediate 'half-applied' state without one real instance of it
